children: Standard BioTools said it agreed to sell its Microfluidics business to Archimed, an investment firm focused exclusively on healthcare industries.
Standard BioTools said Monday its Microfluidics technology enables experiments at a scale that isn't possible with traditional benchtop techniques, resulting in greater precision.
Michael Egholm, the company's president and chief executive, said the deal marks another important step in the strategic actions laid out for Standard BioTools.
Last month, the company said it agreed to sell its Mass Cytometry business to Element Biosystems.
The sale to Archimed is expected to close in about 30 days, Standard BioTools said.
